metadata.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
metadata.authors: Xingchao Liu, Chengyue Gong, Qiang Liu

nodes.name: Transport Mapping Problem
nodes.statement: Given empirical observations of two distributions $X_0 \sim \pi_0$, $X_1 \sim \pi_1$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, find a transport map $T\colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $Z_1 \defeq T(Z_0) \sim \pi_1$ when $Z_0 \sim \pi_0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Given samples from two distributions, find a transport map that pushes one to the other.

nodes.name: Expected Velocity
nodes.statement: For a path-wise continuously differentiable random process $\mathbf{X} = \{X_t\colon t \in [0,1]\}$, its expected velocity is $v^{\mathbf{X}}(x,t) = \mathbb{E}[\dot X_t \mid X_t = x]$ for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(X_t)$.

nodes.name: Rectifiable Process and Rectified Flow
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{X}$ is rectifiable if $v^{\mathbf{X}}$ is locally bounded and the integral equation $Z_t = Z_0 + \int_0^t v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_s, s)\,ds$, $Z_0 = X_0$, has a unique solution; the resulting $\mathbf{Z}$ is the rectified flow induced from $\mathbf{X}$.

nodes.name: Rectifiable Coupling and Rectified Coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0, X_1)$ is rectifiable if its linear interpolation $\mathbf{X} = \{tX_1 + (1-t)X_0\colon t \in [0,1]\}$ is rectifiable. Denote $\mathbf{Z} = \mathrm{rectflow}((X_0, X_1))$ and $(Z_0, Z_1) = \mathrm{rectify}((X_0, X_1))$.

nodes.name: Straight (Fully Rectified) Coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0, X_1)$ is straight (or fully rectified) if it is a fixed point of the $\mathrm{rectify}(\cdot)$ mapping.

nodes.name: Straight Flow
nodes.statement: A flow $dZ_t = v(Z_t, t)\,dt$ is straight if almost surely $Z_t = tZ_1 + (1-t)Z_0$ for all $t \in [0,1]$, equivalently $v(Z_t,t) = Z_1 - Z_0 = \mathrm{const}$ along each path.

nodes.name: Straightness Functional
nodes.statement: The straightness of a continuously differentiable process $\mathbf{Z}$ is $S(\mathbf{Z}) = \int_0^1 \mathbb{E}[\|(Z_1 - Z_0) - \dot Z_t\|^2]\,dt$; $S(\mathbf{Z}) = 0$ iff $\mathbf{Z}$ is exactly straight.

nodes.name: $c$-Optimal Coupling
nodes.statement: A coupling $(X_0, X_1)$ is $c$-optimal if it minimizes $\mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$ among all couplings sharing the same marginals.

nodes.name: Non-Intersection Functional $V$
nodes.statement: $V((X_0,X_1)) := \int_0^1 \mathbb{E}[\|X_1 - X_0 - \mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t]\|^2]\,dt$; $V = 0$ iff the linear interpolation paths do not intersect.

nodes.name: Optimal Velocity Field $v^X$
nodes.statement: $v^X(x, t) = \mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t = x]$.

nodes.name: Closed-Form $v^X$ via Conditional Density
nodes.statement: $v^X(z,t) = \mathbb{E}\left[\frac{X_1 - z}{1 - t}\,\eta_t(X_1, z)\right]$ where $\eta_t(X_1, z) = \rho\!\left(\frac{z - tX_1}{1 - t}\,\big|\,X_1\right) / \mathbb{E}\!\left[\rho\!\left(\frac{z - tX_1}{1-t}\,\big|\,X_1\right)\right]$.

nodes.name: Nadaraya-Watson Estimator of $v^X$
nodes.statement: $v^{X,h}(z,t) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{X_1 - z}{1 - t}\,\omega_h(X_t, z)\right]$ with $\omega_h(X_t,z) = \kappa_h(X_t,z) / \mathbb{E}[\kappa_h(X_t,z)]$ and Gaussian RBF kernel $\kappa_h(x,z) = \exp(-\|x-z\|^2/2h^2)$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear Rectified Flow Objective
nodes.statement: $\min_v \int_0^1 \mathbb{E}[w_t \|v(X_t, t) - \dot X_t\|^2]\,dt$ for any time-differentiable interpolation $X_t$ with $X_0,X_1$ as endpoints.

nodes.name: Inviscid Burgers' Equation for Straight Flow
nodes.statement: If a flow $dZ_t = v(Z_t,t)\,dt$ is straight, then $\partial_t v + (\partial_z v)\,v = 0$.

nodes.name: (sub-)VP ODE Coefficient $\alpha_t$
nodes.statement: $\alpha_t = \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{1}{4}a(1-t)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}b(1-t)\right)$, default $a = 19.9$, $b = 0.1$; VP ODE: $\beta_t = \sqrt{1 - \alpha_t^2}$; sub-VP ODE: $\beta_t = 1 - \alpha_t^2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Song et al. 2020 (Score-Based Generative Modeling through SDEs)

nodes.name: Marginal Preserving Property
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathbf{X}$ is rectifiable and $\mathbf{Z}$ is its rectified flow. Then $\mathrm{law}(Z_t) = \mathrm{law}(X_t)$ for all $t \in [0,1]$.
assumptions: $\mathbf{Z}$ is the rectified flow induced from $\mathbf{X}$
conclusions: In particular, $(Z_0, Z_1)$ is a coupling of $\pi_0, \pi_1$

nodes.name: Reduction of Convex Transport Costs
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_0, X_1)$ is rectifiable and $(Z_0, Z_1) = \mathrm{rectify}((X_0, X_1))$. Then for any convex $c\colon\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] \leq \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$.
assumptions: $(X_0, X_1)$ is a rectifiable coupling of $\pi_0, \pi_1$
conclusions: $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] \leq \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$ (Pareto descent over all convex costs)

nodes.name: Characterization of Straight Couplings
nodes.statement: Assume $(X_0,X_1)$ is rectifiable. Then $(X_0,X_1)$ is straight iff (1) there exists a strictly convex $c$ with $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1-Z_0)] = \mathbb{E}[c(X_1-X_0)]$; iff (2) $(X_0,X_1) = (Z_0,Z_1)$; iff (3) $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{Z}$; iff (4) $V((X_0,X_1)) = 0$.
conclusions: Equivalences (1)-(4) hold; in particular straight iff linear interpolation paths do not intersect ($V = 0$)

nodes.name: $\mathcal{O}(1/K)$ Convergence of Straightening under Reflow
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{Z}^k$ be the $k$-th rectified flow with $(Z_0^0,Z_1^0) = (X_0,X_1)$, each $(Z_0^k,Z_1^k)$ rectifiable. Then $\sum_{k=0}^K (S(\mathbf{Z}^{k+1}) + V((Z_0^k,Z_1^k))) \leq \mathbb{E}[\|X_1 - X_0\|^2]$.

nodes.name: $c$-Optimal Implies Straight
nodes.statement: If a rectifiable coupling $(X_0, X_1)$ is $c$-optimal for some strictly convex cost $c$, then $(X_0, X_1)$ is a straight coupling.
assumptions: $(X_0, X_1)$ is $c$-optimal for some strictly convex $c\colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$

nodes.name: 1D Existence and Uniqueness of Straight Coupling
nodes.statement: For any $\pi_0, \pi_1$ on $\mathbb{R}$, either there is no straight coupling, or there is a unique one. If exists, it is deterministic, monotonic, and jointly optimal w.r.t. all convex costs $c\colon \mathbb{R} \to [0, +\infty)$ with finite optimal value.
conclusions: Either no straight coupling exists, or a unique straight coupling exists
If exists, the unique straight coupling is deterministic and monotonic
It is jointly optimal w.r.t. all convex non-negative cost functions for which the optimum exists

nodes.name: 1D Straight = Deterministic + Monotonic
nodes.statement: A coupling on $\mathbb{R}$ is straight iff it is deterministic and monotonic.

nodes.name: PF-ODEs as Nonlinear Rectified Flows
nodes.statement: Assume the relation $\alpha_t = \exp(\int_t^1 \eta_s\,ds)$, $\beta_t^2 = \int_t^1 \exp(2\int_t^s \eta_r\,dr)\sigma_s^2\,ds$ holds. Then the PF-ODE objective is equivalent to the nonlinear rectified flow objective with $X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \beta_t \xi$, $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$.
conclusions: PF-ODE training objective is equivalent to the nonlinear rectified flow objective with $X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \beta_t \xi$

nodes.name: Proof of Marginal Preserving Property
nodes.statement: Both $\mathrm{law}(X_t)$ and $\mathrm{law}(Z_t)$ solve the same continuity equation $\dot \rho_t + \mathrm{div}(v_t^{\mathbf{X}} \rho_t) = 0$ with the same initial condition; uniqueness gives equality.

nodes.name: Compute time derivative via expected velocity
nodes.statement: For any compactly supported $C^1$ test $h$, $\frac{d}{dt}\mathbb{E}[h(X_t)] = \mathbb{E}[\nabla h(X_t)^\top \dot X_t] = \mathbb{E}[\nabla h(X_t)^\top v^{\mathbf{X}}(X_t,t)]$, using $v^{\mathbf{X}}(X_t,t) = \mathbb{E}[\dot X_t \mid X_t]$.

nodes.name: Identify continuity equation
nodes.statement: By integration by parts, the previous identity is equivalent to $\rho_t \defeq \mathrm{law}(X_t)$ solving $\dot \rho_t + \mathrm{div}(v_t^{\mathbf{X}} \rho_t) = 0$ in the sense of distributions.

nodes.name: Apply uniqueness of continuity equation
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{law}(Z_t)$ satisfies the same continuity equation with the same initial condition $Z_0 = X_0$. Uniqueness (Kurtz 2011 Cor. 1.3; Ambrosio 2008 Thm. 4.1), guaranteed by uniqueness of $dZ_t = v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_t,t)\,dt$, yields $\mathrm{law}(Z_t) = \mathrm{law}(X_t)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Convex Cost Reduction
nodes.statement: Two applications of Jensen's inequality, combined with the marginal-preserving property, give $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] \leq \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$.

nodes.name: Express $Z_1 - Z_0$ as integral of $v^{\mathbf{X}}$ and apply Jensen
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[c\!\left(\int_0^1 v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_t,t)\,dt\right)\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^1 c(v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_t,t))\,dt\right]$ by Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Switch from $Z_t$ to $X_t$ via marginal equality
nodes.statement: Because $\mathrm{law}(X_t) = \mathrm{law}(Z_t)$, we replace $Z_t$ with $X_t$: $\mathbb{E}[\int_0^1 c(v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_t,t))\,dt] = \mathbb{E}[\int_0^1 c(v^{\mathbf{X}}(X_t,t))\,dt]$.

nodes.name: Apply Jensen on conditional expectation defining $v^X$
nodes.statement: Since $v^X(X_t, t) = \mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t]$, Jensen gives $c(\mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t]) \leq \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0) \mid X_t]$. Taking total expectation yields $\mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Straightness Equivalences
nodes.statement: Show $3 \Rightarrow 2 \Rightarrow 1$ trivially, $1 \Rightarrow 4$ via tightness in Jensen with strictly convex $c$, and $4 \Rightarrow 3$ via the integral equation matching $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$.

nodes.name: Trivial directions $3 \Rightarrow 2 \Rightarrow 1$
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{Z} \Rightarrow (X_0,X_1) = (Z_0,Z_1) \Rightarrow$ identical convex-cost expectations for any $c$.

nodes.name: Tightness in Jensen forces $V(\mathbf{X}) = 0$
nodes.statement: Equality $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] = \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$ with strictly convex $c$ forces equality in the second Jensen of the proof of Theorem TP233.2, hence $X_1 - X_0 = \mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t]$ a.s., i.e., $V(\mathbf{X}) = 0$.

nodes.name: $V(\mathbf{X}) = 0 \Rightarrow$ $\mathbf{X}$ solves the rectified-flow ODE
nodes.statement: If $V(\mathbf{X}) = 0$, then $X_t = X_0 + \int_0^t v^X(X_s, s)\,ds$. By uniqueness of the ODE solution, $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{Z}$.

nodes.name: Proof of $\mathcal{O}(1/K)$ Convergence
nodes.statement: Specializing $c(x) = \|x\|^2$ in the proof of cost reduction yields a per-step decrement equal to $S(\mathbf{Z}^{k+1}) + V((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$; telescoping over $k = 0, \ldots, K$ gives the bound.

nodes.name: Quadratic specialization
nodes.statement: Taking $c(x) = \|x\|^2$ in the proof of Theorem TP233.2 yields the identity $\mathbb{E}[\|X_1 - X_0\|^2] - \mathbb{E}[\|Z_1 - Z_0\|^2] = S(\mathbf{Z}) + V((X_0, X_1))$.

nodes.name: Telescoping sum over reflow iterations
nodes.statement: Applying the per-step identity to each $k$ and summing $k = 0, \ldots, K$ gives $\sum_k (S(\mathbf{Z}^{k+1}) + V((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))) \leq \mathbb{E}[\|X_1 - X_0\|^2]$.

nodes.name: Proof of $c$-Optimal $\Rightarrow$ Straight
nodes.statement: Let $(Z_0,Z_1) = \mathrm{rectify}((X_0,X_1))$. $c$-optimality forces $\mathbb{E}[c(Z_1 - Z_0)] = \mathbb{E}[c(X_1 - X_0)]$, which by Theorem TP233.3 (Statement 1) yields straightness.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP233.1 (1D Straight = Deterministic Monotonic)
nodes.statement: Forward: straightness $\Rightarrow$ coincides with rectified coupling, which is deterministic by ODE construction and monotonic by the non-crossing property of flows. Reverse: monotonicity $\Rightarrow$ no path crossings $\Rightarrow$ $X_t$ solves the rectified-flow ODE uniquely $\Rightarrow$ straight by Theorem TP233.3 statement 3.

nodes.name: Straight $\Rightarrow$ deterministic and monotonic
nodes.statement: If $(X_0,X_1)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is straight, it equals its rectified coupling $(Z_0,Z_1)$ which is deterministic (induced by ODE) and monotonic (non-crossing of solutions).

nodes.name: Deterministic monotonic $\Rightarrow$ straight
nodes.statement: Monotonicity implies linear interpolation paths do not intersect, so $X_1 - X_0 = \mathbb{E}[X_1 - X_0 \mid X_t] = v^X(X_t, t)$ on $(0,1)$. Hence $X_t$ solves the rectified-flow ODE; uniqueness and Theorem TP233.3 (statement 3) give straightness.

nodes.name: Proof of 1D Existence/Uniqueness Theorem
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma LP233.1 with Lemma 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 of Santambrogio (2015), which establish uniqueness and joint optimality of the 1D monotonic coupling for all convex costs.

nodes.name: Proof of PF-ODE / Rectified-Flow Equivalence
nodes.statement: Show $\dot X_t = \tilde Y_t$ by substituting the relations $\eta_t = -\dot \alpha_t/\alpha_t$ and $\sigma_t^2 = 2\beta_t^2(\dot\alpha_t/\alpha_t - \dot\beta_t/\beta_t)$ implied by the integral relation $\alpha_t = \exp(\int_t^1 \eta_s\,ds)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $V_t = X_t$
nodes.statement: Take $\xi_t = \xi$ for all $t$; then $V_t = X_t = \alpha_t X_1 + \beta_t \xi$.

nodes.name: Algebraic simplification of $\tilde Y_t$
nodes.statement: Expand $\tilde Y_t = -\eta_t X_t + \frac{\sigma_t^2}{2\beta_t^2}(\alpha_t X_1 - X_t)$ and substitute the relations $\eta_t = -\dot\alpha_t/\alpha_t$ and $\sigma_t^2 = 2\beta_t^2(\dot\alpha_t/\alpha_t - \dot\beta_t/\beta_t)$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\tilde Y_t = \dot X_t$
nodes.statement: After substitution, $\tilde Y_t = \dot \alpha_t X_1 + \dot \beta_t \xi = \dot X_t$, completing the equivalence.

nodes.name: Rectified Flow Main Algorithm (rectflow)
nodes.statement: Iterative training-and-sampling procedure that computes the rectified flow $\mathbf{Z} = \mathrm{rectflow}((X_0,X_1))$ by minimizing the linear-interpolation least-squares objective and simulating the resulting ODE.
input: Draws from a coupling $(X_0, X_1)$ of $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$

nodes.name: Initialize velocity model
nodes.statement: Initialize neural network $v_\theta$ with parameter $\theta$.

nodes.name: Train: minimize least-squares objective
nodes.statement: $\hat\theta = \arg\min_\theta \mathbb{E}[\|X_1 - X_0 - v_\theta(tX_1 + (1-t)X_0,\,t)\|^2]$ with $t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}([0,1])$, via SGD/Adam over draws of $(X_0,X_1)$.

nodes.name: Sample by Euler ODE solver
nodes.statement: Draw $(Z_0, Z_1)$ by simulating $dZ_t = v_{\hat\theta}(Z_t, t)\,dt$ from $Z_0 \sim \pi_0$ (forward) or $Z_1 \sim \pi_1$ (backward) using Euler / RK45 solver.

nodes.name: Return rectified flow
nodes.statement: Return $\mathbf{Z} = \{Z_t\colon t \in [0,1]\}$.

nodes.name: Reflow
nodes.statement: Recursive application of $\mathrm{rectflow}$: $\mathbf{Z}^{k+1} = \mathrm{rectflow}((Z_0^k, Z_1^k))$ starting from $(Z_0^0, Z_1^0) = (X_0, X_1)$, producing increasingly straight $k$-rectified flows.

nodes.name: Loop over reflow iterations
nodes.statement: For $k = 1, \ldots, K$: train $v$ on the current coupling via $\mathrm{rectflow}$ and resample to obtain $(Z_0^k, Z_1^k)$.

nodes.name: Distillation of $k$-Rectified Flow
nodes.statement: Train a one-step network $\hat T(z_0) = z_0 + v(z_0, 0)$ to predict $Z_1^k$ from $Z_0^k$, by minimizing $\mathbb{E}[\|(Z_1^k - Z_0^k) - v(Z_0^k, 0)\|^2]$ on draws from $(Z_0^k, Z_1^k)$.
output: One-step model $\hat T$ such that $Z_1^k \approx \hat T(Z_0^k)$

nodes.name: Non-Parametric Velocity Estimator
nodes.statement: Nadaraya-Watson kernel estimator $v^{X,h}(z,t)$ approximates the optimal $v^X$ in low dimensions using top-$m$ nearest neighbors with Gaussian RBF kernel of bandwidth $h$.

nodes.name: Probability Flow ODE / DDIM
nodes.statement: ODE-based generative model derived as the deterministic counterpart of a learned score-based SDE; trained via denoising score matching with hyperparameter sequences $\alpha_t, \beta_t$ derived from the SDE drift/diffusion.
nodes.origin_citation: Song et al. 2020 (Score-Based SDE); Song et al. 2020 (DDIM); Ho et al. 2020 (DDPM)

nodes.name: Toy 2D Distributions (Two-dot, Star, Circle)
nodes.statement: Illustration of rectified flow and reflow on synthetic 2D distributions: trajectories of $X_t$ and $Z_t$ shown to demonstrate path rewiring at intersection points and straightening with successive reflow steps.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 Unconditional Image Generation
nodes.statement: Rectified flow with DDPM++ U-Net architecture achieves FID 4.85 (with distillation) and recall 0.51 on CIFAR-10 with one Euler step, state-of-the-art for one-step fast diffusion/flow models.

nodes.name: Image-to-Image Translation (AFHQ, MetFace, CelebA-HQ)
nodes.statement: Rectified flow applied to unpaired image translation between human and animal faces using $\pi_0$ as source domain and $\pi_1$ as target domain.

nodes.name: Comparison with VP / sub-VP ODE on Gaussian-to-Mixture
nodes.statement: On 2D toy with $\pi_0 = \mathcal{N}(0,I)$ and $\pi_1$ a low-variance Gaussian mixture, linear rectified flow yields nearly straight trajectories after one reflow, while VP/sub-VP ODE remain curved with non-uniform speed.

nodes.name: Non-Crossing Property of Flows
nodes.statement: Distinct paths of a well-posed ODE $dZ_t = v(Z_t, t)\,dt$ cannot cross at any $t \in [0,1)$; the rectified flow rewires intersecting linear-interpolation paths to obey this property while preserving marginals.

nodes.name: Causalization, Markovianization, Derandomization
nodes.statement: While $X_t$ is generally non-causal and non-Markov with stochastic coupling $(X_0, X_1)$, the rectified flow $Z_t$ causalizes, Markovianizes, and derandomizes $X_t$ while preserving all marginal laws.

nodes.name: Distillation $\neq$ Rectification
nodes.statement: Distillation faithfully approximates the existing coupling $(Z_0^k, Z_1^k)$, whereas rectification yields a different coupling $(Z_0^{k+1}, Z_1^{k+1})$ with lower transport cost and more straight flow; distillation is best applied as the final fine-tuning stage.

nodes.name: Smoothing of Singular $X_0 \mid X_1$
nodes.statement: When $X_0 \mid X_1$ has no conditional density, $v^X$ may be undefined or discontinuous; adding Gaussian noise $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I)$ to $X_0$ smooths the problem and yields a randomized transport.

nodes.name: Multi-Dimensional: Straight $\neq$ $c$-Optimal
nodes.statement: On $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, straight couplings are not guaranteed to be $c$-optimal for any specific $c$; this matches the design that $\mathrm{rectify}(\cdot)$ does not target a specific cost.
